name: Erste Group Bank AG
reason: Solid CEE retail bank (10y avg ROE 12%, EPS EUR 3.08 in 2016 to 4.26 in 2021 through zero rates) but 2025 EPS of EUR 8.23 is a peak-NIM 10y high and the 2025 purchase of 49% of Santander Bank Polska is a transformational deal whose integration and Polish bank-tax/CHF-mortgage exposure cannot be forecast with confidence.

name: National Bank of Greece SA
reason: Greek turnaround bank with EPS EUR -3.95 (2015) to 1.38 (2025) driven by NPL clean-up and rate tailwind, 10y avg ROE 8.1% and flat 10y revenue; earnings set by the rate/credit cycle with no through-cycle record.

name: Retail Estates SA
reason: Belgian/Dutch out-of-town retail REIT with FFO per share only EUR 5.13 (FY2017) to 6.15 (FY2025), consensus FY1-FY3 growth ~1%, share count +5.5%/yr and net debt/EBITDA 7.1x; regulated-REIT payout leaves no route to 7% growth.

name: Industrivarden AB
reason: Swedish investment holding company whose reported EPS (SEK 82 in 2025 vs -32 in 2022 and -19 in 2018) is mark-to-market on a listed portfolio, so earnings are set by equity markets rather than an operating business; express via the underlying holdings or index instead.

name: Nordea Bank Abp
reason: Large Nordic bank whose EPS went nowhere through the zero-rate years (EUR 0.88 in 2016 to 0.95 in 2021) and only rose to 1.39-1.44 on the rate cycle; 10y EPS CAGR 4.3% and FY2-FY3 consensus 7-9% make it cheap-but-ordinary rather than best-in-class.

name: Aktia Bank Plc
reason: Small Finnish bank with 10y EPS CAGR 4.0% (EUR 0.77 to 1.15), 10y avg ROE 8.5% and FY2-FY3 consensus growth of 3-6%; fails the bank standard on ROE and growth.

name: Bank of Ireland Group Plc
reason: Irish bank with EPS EUR 0.70 (2015) to 1.15 (2025) including a 2020 loss, 10y avg ROE 7.2% and 2016-21 EPS falling; earnings set by rates and Irish credit, not a through-cycle compounder.

name: ArcelorMittal SA
reason: Global steel producer with EPS swinging from USD -10.17 (2015) to 13.49 (2021) to 1.09 (2023) and EBIT margin 0.9-21.9%; earnings set by steel spreads (commodity).

name: BPER Banca SpA
reason: Italian bank whose EPS jump from EUR 0.21 (2021) to 1.09 (2025) came from rates and serial acquisitions (Carige, UBI branches, Pop Sondrio) with shares outstanding +8.9%/yr and 10y avg ROE 9.7%; growth via M&A and the rate cycle.

name: Bell Food Group AG
reason: Coop-controlled Swiss meat processor with EBIT margin of 2.4-5.6%, EPS CHF 22.01 (2016) down to 11.10 (2025), 10y avg ROIC 5.2% and acquisitions 1.8x FCF; low-return commodity food processing with no specialness.

name: Cordiant Digital Infrastructure Ltd.
reason: Guernsey closed-end fund holding CEE towers/data centres whose 'EPS' (GBP 0.07-0.21) is mainly NAV revaluation gains with zero FCF conversion to shareholders; not a forecastable operating earnings stream.

name: Mapfre SA
reason: Fundacion-controlled multiline insurer with 10y EPS CAGR 4.7% (EUR 0.23 to 0.36), 10y avg ROE 8.6%, heavy Latam/Brazil FX and cat exposure and consensus LTG 5.2%; cheap-but-ordinary with no route to 7%.

name: Bank Polska Kasa Opieki SA
reason: State-controlled (PZU/PFR) Polish bank whose EPS tripled from PLN 5.81 (2022) to 27.69 (2025) purely on rates after flat 2015-21 (~PLN 8-9), with bank tax and government policy risk and consensus FY1 -18%; peak-NIM earnings.

name: JBS NV
reason: Global meatpacker with EPS USD 0.00 (2018) to 1.71 (2021) to -0.09 (2023) to 1.89 (2025) set by the cattle/hog/chicken cycle, net debt/EBITDA 2.8x and a Batista-family governance record (J&F bribery settlements).

name: ING Groep NV
reason: Large European bank with EPS flat through the zero-rate years (EUR 1.22 in 2016 to 1.23 in 2021), 10y revenue CAGR 1.9% and 10y avg ROE 9.7%; 2023-25 EPS of ~EUR 2 is rate-driven and growth comes mainly from buybacks.

name: St. James's Place Plc
reason: UK advice-led wealth manager with good record (EPS GBP 0.38 in 2016 to 0.86 in 2025, ROE 21%) but earnings track market levels and net flows, and the 2025 fee-structure overhaul plus ~GBP 500m ongoing-advice refund provision under FCA Consumer Duty make 5-10y economics hard to forecast.

name: M&G Plc
reason: UK asset manager/life insurer with GAAP EPS of GBP 0.41 (2019) falling to losses in 2022 and 2024 and 0.12 in 2025, 10y avg ROE 3.2% and persistent asset-management outflows; earnings set by markets and with-profits/annuity accounting.

name: NEPI Rockcastle NV
reason: CEE shopping-mall owner with FFO per share EUR ~0.55 (2018) to 0.60 (2024), net debt/EBITDA 4.9x, acquisitions 0.47x FCF and FY2-FY3 consensus ~5%; property cycle with no route to 7% growth.

name: SSAB AB
reason: Swedish steelmaker with EPS SEK -0.62 (2015) to 22.38 (2022) to 4.92 (2025) and EBIT margin -2.9% to 19.8%; earnings set by steel prices plus large HYBRIT/Lulea fossil-free capex that turns NTM FCF yield to -5.8%.

name: Sava Re dd
reason: Slovenian reinsurer/insurer with an impressive record (GAAP EPS EUR 2.02 in 2015 to 7.35 in 2025, worst year -10.6%, 10y ROE 13.6%) but 2025 is a 10y high helped by investment yields, the Slovenian state (SDH) is a large shareholder, and the small Adriatic/Balkan franchise and reinsurance cat exposure limit long-range forecastability.
